title: 1958 AHSME Problem 21
statement: In the accompanying figure \(\overline{CE}\) and \(\overline{DE}\) are equal chords of a circle with center \(O.\) Arc \(AB\) is a quarter-circle. Then the ratio of the area of triangle \(CED\) to the area of triangle \(AOB\) is:

solutions.text:
Let the circle have radius \(r.\) In the pictured configuration, \(\overline{CD}\) is a diameter and \(E\) is the endpoint of the perpendicular radius, so \[ [CED]=\frac12(2r)(r)=r^2. \] Since arc \(AB\) is a quarter-circle, \(\angle AOB=90^\circ,\) and \[ [AOB]=\frac12r^2. \] The requested ratio is therefore \(2:1.\)

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: The equal chords from \(E\) make the pictured triangle symmetric about the perpendicular diameter
Compare each triangle’s base-height area in terms of the circle radius
